candidates.detail: The public Replicon postcard helper accepts any bytes::Buf. Its flavor checks remaining() >= ct, then forms a ct-length raw slice from chunk().as_ptr() and advances. The pinned bytes Buf contract permits chunk() to be shorter than remaining(), and Chain returns the first component chunk while summing both remaining lengths. Rust slice construction requires the full range to be valid in one allocation. Thus the check alone cannot establish the unsafe slice precondition for all permitted Buf values.
candidates.conditional_case: For separately allocated one-byte and three-byte slices combined using the pinned bytes Chain, a call through the public helper to deserialize f32 would have remaining=4 and first chunk length=1. Serde dispatches f32 to postcard deserialize_f32, whose four-byte temporary read delegates by default to this flavor try_take_n. The code would form a four-byte slice from the one-byte allocation, violating the raw-slice safety contract. This is source reasoning only; no decoder, unsafe operation or memory fault was executed or observed. Features and compilation remain unverified.
candidates.safeguards: The personally inspected current tactical SceneBuilding decoder takes &mut bytes::Bytes, and the inspected native message and component callback signatures also use Bytes. In the pinned bytes source, Bytes::remaining returns its length and Bytes::chunk returns its entire slice, so the fragmented Chain example does not apply to those concrete signatures. This is a bounded safeguard, not proof of all lifetime safety, every helper caller, all compiled features, or absence of a different product path. No remote exploit or product vulnerability is established.
